absence_evidence.key_result: Loosened near miss by name and by project family: across every AQUAEXCEL-prefixed project, no coordinator is Norwegian by country code or by organisation name.

absence_evidence.key_result: The near miss sits next to something real: Norway is on AQUAEXCEL3.0 through four organisations - HAVFORSKNINGSINSTITUTTET, NOFIMA AS, NORGES TEKNISK-NATURVITENSKAPELIGE UNIVERSITET NTNU, SINTEF OCEAN AS - every one of them a participant.

reference_answer: No Norwegian organisation coordinates AQUAEXCEL3.0 - the project's coordinator is INSTITUT NATIONAL DE RECHERCHE POUR L'AGRICULTURE, L'ALIMENTATION ET L'ENVIRONNEMENT, based in France. Norway is present on the project only as four participants: HAVFORSKNINGSINSTITUTTET, NOFIMA AS, NORGES TEKNISK-NATURVITENSKAPELIGE UNIVERSITET NTNU and SINTEF OCEAN AS.
notes: Absence claim: AQUAEXCEL3.0 exists and has exactly one coordinator, and that coordinator is not Norwegian - it is INRAE (FR); no Norwegian organisation on the project holds a coordinating role under any grain. Parent sql-04 ('Which organisation is the coordinator of the AQUAEXCEL3.0 project?') was re-executed this pass and still returns INSTITUT NATIONAL DE RECHERCHE POUR L'AGRICULTURE, L'ALIMENTATION ET L'ENVIRONNEMENT. Edit from parent: one word inserted - the nationality 'Norwegian' - which distorts the very fact the parent's gold establishes. Subtype fit: false-presupposition, not zero-match - the refutation is positive ('the data says the coordinator is French INRAE'), not merely an empty count, and the subject entity exists; the facet (role, country) is fully carried by the schema, so it is not data-absent either. Plausibility: Norway is the dominant European aquaculture research nation and four Norwegian institutes (Havforskningsinstituttet, Nofima, NTNU, SINTEF Ocean) really are on this aquaculture-infrastructure project, so a user asking this in good faith is entirely realistic. Near miss verified in both directions: the Norwegian-coordinator queries return nothing under country code, under organisation-name matching, under the alternate coordinator grain (participantOrder=1, non-participant roles) and across the whole AQUAEXCEL project family, while the Norwegian-participant query returns four rows. Sibling check: AQUAEXCEL2020 is coordinated by the same French INRAE, so there is no adjacent project that would make the premise true. No search_corpus sweep was run: the protocol requires the semantic sweep for zero-match, and this premise is settled entirely on stored structured columns (organization.role, organization.country). schema_docs_hash f8c001e8cc8f recorded because the proof leans on the value notes for organization.role and the 'coordinator is always participantOrder 1' note.

reference_answer: No EU-funded project in this corpus studies nineteenth-century business or corporate efforts to influence government policy; nothing matches this question. The corpus's research on business influence over policy is contemporary or late-twentieth-century (BUSWEL, PROSPER, TRASC, BIZPOL, EFTA DEVELOPMENT on 1958-1992), and its nineteenth-century projects (TRANSPOP on popular politics, WARCAP on fiscal capacity and warfare, J-INNOVATECH on Japanese industrialisation) do not study business influence on policy.
notes: ABSENCE CLAIM: no project in the corpus researches efforts by businesses, firms, corporations or industry to influence the policies or regulations adopted by governments in the nineteenth century - neither in project.objective nor in any report_text section. PARENT AND EDIT: parent vec-15 'Which EU-funded projects study how companies and business groups try to influence the policies and regulations that governments adopt?' (L3 survey, 16 gold). One thing changed: the period, by inserting 'nineteenth-century' before the actor and putting the verbs in the past tense. Actor, action and target are the parent's, word for word. SUBTYPE FIT: zero-match, not data-absent - the facet (what a project studies, as stated in its own free text) is exactly what the parent question is answered from, and the parent returns 16 projects on it; what is missing is the instance, a nineteenth-century case. Not false-presupposition: the question presupposes nothing that the data contradicts, it simply has no members. NON-SQL PROOF - semantic sweep: search_corpus(question text, condition='pooled', k=20) over lexical, dense, hybrid and hybrid_rerank (index be84cbad9182) returned 38 distinct projects; every one adjudicated OFF-TOPIC, in two clean families. (a) Business influence on policy, but present-day: 705677 BUSWEL, 834253 TRASC, 865165 CORPORATOCRACY (all parent gold), 101026008 REGTRUST, 870722 TiGRE, 789013 OCIAN, 793639 PEDAS, 846270 PARTOWNEU, 747947 EU-Drones, 101033472 Tran-Reg, 639084 LEGALARCHITECTURES, 709386 SRR, 660245 GLONEXACO, 674888 TAX4INNO, 649351 IIT, 789461 SCOM, 727524 ENABLE.EU, 817619 AURES II, 101000216 Code Re-farm, 861034 MARKETS, 786641 SHERPA, 843825 FINGOV, 649456 ENLIGHTEN, 892444 EUDIC, 947654 IDED. (b) Nineteenth-century, but not about business influencing policy: 850742 T-MIGRANTS (theatre migrants), 648429 TRANSPOP (popular politics and ordinary people's mobilisation, 1789-1914 - the actor is the public, not business), 752163 WARCAP (fiscal capacity and warfare 1789-1913), 805098 J-INNOVATECH (Japan's industrial technical culture 1800-1885), 757291 CALLIOPE (parliamentary oratory and empire), 101022204 INVCULTURALDIPLO (cultural diplomacy 1870-1940, states not firms), 750690 GASAC, 101026870 MIRMINT, 793204 USPAIN, 840686 FED, 101027394 HuDig19 (all literary/cultural history), 693512 GEPPS (twentieth-century economic unions), 892383 RESCATA (Amazon ecology, retrieval noise). No candidate combines the two, which is the shape the near-miss requires: the retrieval stack returns plausible neighbours on both sides of the missing cell rather than nothing at all. NON-SQL PROOF - reads: three period-marked candidates found by SQL sweeps were read in full and rejected. 795823 OilandEmp ('British oil imperialism and the making of the modern Middle East, c.1901-c.1935') is early twentieth century and argues that 'british state and business interests were at the forefront of this new coercive interventionism' - joint state-business imperial expansion abroad, not business influence on domestic policy, and the wrong century. 695573 COLOUR (racialization of nineteenth-century indentured migrant labour) contains no policy-influence claim. 101025880 PETITIA studies Dutch merchants petitioning the Amsterdam city council - the closest thing in the corpus to the asked-for research, and explicitly seventeenth century ('predating the nineteenth century'). REMAINING DOUBT, disclosed: 833834 Water-Cultures ('The Water Cultures of Italy, 1500-1900') is the one row of the widest sweep. Its work-stream list includes 'the efforts of social actors, including water companies, municipalities, private entrepreneurs, technicians and users, to regulate access, use and distribution of water in 19th-century italian cities'. It was adjudicated OFF-TOPIC because the project is a social and cultural history of human-water interaction and the stream describes participation in water provision and management, not an effort to influence policies or regulations that a government adopts; a stricter reader could argue it is a marginal match. reference_answer: The database carries no proposal-evaluation facet: no table or column in it holds an evaluation, score, panel or ranking field, and none of the seven glaciology projects starting in 2021 or later - including the one meant here, DEEPICE (grant 955750) - records a score anywhere in its title, objective or report sections. What is stored for DEEPICE is its status (CLOSED), its funding (ecMaxContribution EUR 4,166,057.88, totalCost EUR 4,166,057.88) and its free-text objective and report, so the evaluation score its proposal received cannot be answered from this data.
notes: ABSENCE CLAIM (scoped to what was executed): the schema carries no evaluation/score/panel/ranking/assessment/review column in any table, and none of the 7 filter survivors - DEEPICE included - records a proposal score anywhere in title, objective, teaser, summary, workPerformed or finalResults under a wide score-phrasing set; so the score awarded to DEEPICE's proposal is unavailable. SCOPE DISCLOSURE (raised by the critic, upheld by the judge): the corpus at large is NOT free of proposal scores. Nine projects state their own score in stored text - objective: 696898 WELL 'achieving a total score of 12,88', 717497 ECOBREW2 'evaluated with a score of 12.81 and awarded with the Seal of Excellence', 728455 SAP-Nano 'a total score of 12,84', 739013 Smart OEE 'with a total score of 13.95', 744040 ECOMOBI 'the Seal of Excellence label ... with a score of 13.28', 761883 MePlat 'received a score of 13.71', 954038 ROBOHARVEST 'a Seal of Excellence and a score of 13.88'; report_text: 763635 MedSTACH 'The MedSTACH proposal was ranked 1st (score of 15/15) on a pan-European scale, among 208 proposals', 101029605 SAFE-FACE '15/15 perfect score'. The same aggregate finds 84 rows containing 'seal of excellence' and 15 containing 'evaluation panel'. None of these is a glaciology 2021+ survivor and none is DEEPICE; the string 'DEEPICE' appears only in project 955750.
